attempts.paper_title: Causal evidence of a line attractor encoding an affective state.
attempts.entry_title: Line attractor dynamics and holographic perturbation in VMHvl (Vinograd, Nair et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: The paper's group photostimulation results hold in this data: activating x1 neurons drives integration along the x1 dimension, and activating x2 neurons does not. The slow integration dimension that defines the line attractor in rSLDS fits did not reproduce, with x1 slower than x2 in 5 of 7 two-photon mice; the paper's fitted models are not deposited, and new fits change with the random seed. That stimulation moves activity along the attractor holds only in part. The single-neuron stimulation and connectivity findings could not be tested because those sessions are not in the dataset, and the network model could not be run as the Methods describe it. Smaller claims on neuron overlap and variance explained did not reproduce.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Vinograd, Nair, Kim, Linderman and Anderson (2024) on dandiset 001037, which holds miniscope traces and behaviour annotations of 5 freely behaving mice engaging in and observing aggression, and two-photon observation and group photostimulation sessions of 7 head-fixed mice with stored rSLDS factor weights. It fits rSLDS models with the authors' sample-code settings, cross-validates them, tests integration under holographic activation of x1 and x2 neurons, and recomputes the excitatory network model of Figure 4. The unitary stimulation, 1 mW, random-neuron and combined sessions, cell positions and face video are not in the dandiset.

The random-frame folds were not run, as ssm's initialization fails with masked frames; the in-sample reconstruction, which no held-out reading of the neural R2 can be expected to exceed, explains 51.0% and 54.2% (rslds_fits.ipynb, best of four seeds the same), below both expected values. findings.statement: The dandiset holds 7 two-photon mice (M70, M168, M174, M179, M18R, M79RL, M99RL) where the paper reports 9 for observation (Fig. 1) and 8 for x1 group activation; 8 s ISI sessions exist for 6 mice (x1) and 4 (x2) where the paper reports 7.

Not in the dandiset: the unitary (single-neuron) stimulation sessions behind Fig. 3, Fig. 4a, Fig. 5 and Extended Data Figs 10 and 12; the 1 mW, random-neuron and x1-then-x2 stimulation sessions; cell positions or ROI masks; the face video or motion SVDs; the photostimulation calibration recordings. 25 of the 54 claims are blocked as data missing, ed1m for a missing annotation and two through a blocked claim they depend on.

No rSLDS model is stored for the miniscope sessions and only the factor weights are stored for the two-photon sessions (no dynamics matrices, so no time constants); the miniscope files mark no x1 or x2 neurons. The paper's time constants, line attractor scores and miniscope x1 neurons can only be approached by new fits, which differ from seed to seed.

In sub-M70_ses-20230323_behavior.nwb the five neurons listed in ActivatedNeurons for activation_integration_neurons do not respond at the stimulation onsets (-0.01 z, against 0.27 to 0.80 z in the other six mice, and -0.08 to 0.04 z with the indices shifted by -2 to +2) and rank 33rd to 55th of 65 by the stored x1 weight. The cells that respond most are cells 1, 2, 3, 5 and 22, which rank 2nd, 4th, 1st, 8th and 64th by the stored x1 weight, so the weights match the activity and the M70 target list does not. The outcomes of ed7f-activated-x1-natural-levels (M70 left out) and ed8gi-x1-stim-no-x2 (M70 kept) depend on how M70 is treated.

sub-M70/sub-M70_ses-None_behavior.nwb is the same recording as the observation session in sub-M70/sub-M70_ses-20230323_behavior.nwb (per-cell correlation median 0.965 over the first 3000 frames) with different factor weights; the later file stops the session at 300 s (3000 frames), during the second BALB/c visit, while the earlier file holds 4426 frames (443 s), with that visit ending at 350 s.

The miniscope sessions start 56 to 96 s before the first annotation and hold no 5 min solitary baseline, which the Methods say was recorded at the start of every session; the files do not say how they were cropped.

Sniffing of the SW mouse during observation is annotated only for M30L; the other miniscope files keep three of the original behaviour rows (Balb/c, SW, Watch_attack), so Extended Data Fig. 1m (4 mice) cannot be tested. Only M70 among the two-photon mice has BALB/c presence intervals for its observation session; the others hold one entry marker.

That the cells of the engaging and observation sessions of a miniscope mouse are the same cells is not stated in the files, though the paper compares single-cell weights across the two (Extended Data Fig. 4). The files hold the same number of cells in both sessions and no masks; each cell's autocorrelation at a 5 s lag agrees across the sessions (Spearman r 0.35 to 0.61 over cells), which is consistent with matched cells.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors (methods-cvr2): how is the cross-validated R2 of 84.7% and 67.2% computed? Activity reconstructed from the inferred two-dimensional latents of held-out contiguous blocks explains -81% and -75% of the variance about each block's mean and 12.5% and 19.8% about the session mean, and even in sample the reconstruction explains 51% and 54%; which quantity, folds (contiguous or random frames) and baseline give the reported values?

The excitatory network of the Methods (W_ij ~ U(0, 1/N), subnetwork W_ij ~ U(0, 1/N_p), N = 1000, N_p = 200) has a largest eigenvalue of 0.48 to 0.52 at every subnetwork density from 0 to 20%, so it is never unstable and gives tau_n of about 40 s at tau_s = 20 s, while Fig. 4c shows unstable networks and tau_n of 50 to 200 s at 8 to 12%. Question for the authors: how were the weights scaled (a gain, a density-dependent normalization)?

Questions for the authors on choices the paper leaves open: the test behind Fig. 1m (paired or unpaired over mice; the paired test was adopted), the ISI window of Extended Data Fig. 8b (end of pulse to next onset, or onset to onset; the two disagree), and the seed or model selection of the rSLDS fits (seed 0 was adopted; the decoding results of Extended Data Fig. 3g,h depend on it, and with the engaging model's own weights Fig. 3h holds for one of four seeds). Also open: how transient amplitude is measured in Extended Data Fig. 4h (0.58 z is below the 1.5 SD detection threshold), and how the trials are balanced for the decoder.

The sample code's rslds() function ignores its num_iters argument and always runs 150 Laplace-EM iterations, while its miniscope notebooks pass 100; the fits here use 100 for the miniscope, as the notebooks state.

entries.title: Line attractor dynamics and holographic perturbation in VMHvl (Vinograd, Nair et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Vinograd, Nair, Kim, Linderman and Anderson (2024) on dandiset 001037, which holds miniscope traces and behaviour annotations of 5 freely behaving mice engaging in and observing aggression, and two-photon observation and group photostimulation sessions of 7 head-fixed mice with stored rSLDS factor weights. It fits rSLDS models with the authors' sample-code settings, cross-validates them, tests integration under holographic activation of x1 and x2 neurons, and recomputes the excitatory network model of Figure 4. The unitary stimulation, 1 mW, random-neuron and combined sessions, cell positions and face video are not in the dandiset.
